forecasts.name: Climate Pessimist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Rice has already shot to $466 amid El Niño-driven Asian heat and Mediterranean irrigation deficits. Exceeding $500 by March is almost certain.

forecasts.name: Land-Grab Realist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Rice is already at $466, powered by El Niño weather shocks across Asia and sovereign stockpiling. Surpassing $500/mt by March is highly likely.

forecasts.name: IMF (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Strong El Niño risks Asian crop yields, maintaining upward pressure on global cereal benchmarks and straining import-dependent regions.

forecasts.name: BirdLife Europe, EEB, WWF and Greenpeace (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Warming waters and severe drought in major rice basins limit global resilience, maintaining upward price pressure toward $500.

forecasts.name: Macro / Dollar · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Rice is riding a massive multi-quarter upsurge alongside grains; broad macro tailwinds make breaching $500 very plausible.

forecasts.name: FAO (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Strong El Nino conditions historically threaten Asian monsoon dynamics, keeping global rice availability tight and prices well supported.

forecasts.name: Geopolitics Hawk · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Rice is the primary tool of food nationalism. As Asian states expand domestic assistance and manage reserves, global supply remains volatile.

forecasts.name: Crowd Follower · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Market is at 53%. Rice prices have demonstrated a solid upward trend through September, supporting a minor positive tilt.

forecasts.name: Copa-Cogeca (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Large-scale Indian exports limit gains, but weather anomalies and strong Asian domestic demand provide an underlying floor.

forecasts.name: USDA WASDE (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Ample Indian export supplies entering global channels will provide downward pressure on international rice balances, capping rallies above $500/mt.

forecasts.name: IFPRI (Joseph Glauber) (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: India's massive export availability and competitive pricing ease global grain complex strains, restraining international rice prices from sustaining above $500/mt.

forecasts.name: Scott Irwin (farmdoc) (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Surging Indian export volume will weigh heavily on international benchmarks. Supply responses reliably cap price rallies above $500.

forecasts.name: European Commission DG AGRI (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Surging Indian export competition and expanding Asian availability weigh on global trade benchmarks, limiting gains.

forecasts.name: Agronomist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Asian Kharif harvest arrives in force through year-end with record Indian export availability, which seasonally undercuts global import prices and caps gains near $500.

forecasts.name: Adaptation Optimist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Record Indian export supplies and expanding Asian harvests ensure ample global trade availability, tempering price gains.

forecasts.name: Efficient-Market Skeptic · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Rice's run to $466 faces strong headwinds from heavy Indian export supplies. Expecting a further spike above $500 ignores incoming supply pressure.
